title: Degrees of Comparison
description: Master degrees of comparison for Grade 7: comparative structures (as...as, less...than), special adjectives, and transformation between the three degrees — with practice and tests.

topics.title: Comparative Structures & Special Adjectives
topics.concept:
Beyond the simple -er/-est, useful comparison structures include:

  • as … as (equal): She is as tall as her brother.
  • not as … as (less): He is not as fast as me.
  • less … than (lower degree): This is less useful than that.
  • the … the … (parallel change): The harder you work, the more you earn.

Special adjective pairs to watch:

PairUse
elder / olderelder for family; older for all
farther / furtherfarther = distance; further = extra/more
later / latterlater = time; latter = second of two
nearest / nextnearest = distance; next = order

examples.solution: elder — 'elder' is used for family members (and only before a noun).

examples.problem: Rewrite with 'as … as': He is taller than me.
examples.solution: I am not as tall as he is.

recap: Structures: as…as, not as…as, less…than, the…the…
elder/older, farther/further, later/latter, nearest/next have different uses
'elder' and 'eldest' are used only with family and before a noun

topics.title: Transformation Between Degrees
topics.concept:
The same comparison can be written in three ways without changing the meaning. Learn the patterns:

Superlative → Comparative → Positive

  • Superlative: Iron is the most useful metal.
  • Comparative: Iron is more useful than any other metal.
  • Positive: No other metal is as useful as iron.

Key tips:

  • In the comparative form, add 'any other' when comparing one with the rest of its group.
  • In the positive form, start with 'No other …' and use as … as.
  • 'Very few … as … as' shows the top group: Very few metals are as useful as iron.

examples.problem: Change to comparative: Mumbai is one of the largest cities.
examples.solution: Mumbai is larger than most other cities.

examples.problem: Change to positive: Ravi is the tallest boy in the class.
examples.solution: No other boy in the class is as tall as Ravi.

recap: Superlative ↔ comparative ('more … than any other') ↔ positive ('No other … as … as')
Use 'any other' to compare one with its own group

questions.q: Comparative of 'bad':
Choose: 'She is ___ than her friend.'
options: Both A and B are acceptable
questions.explanation: Two-syllable adjectives like 'clever' accept both 'cleverer' and 'more clever'.

questions.q: 'No other boy is ___ tall ___ Ravi.'
'My ___ brother is married.' (family)
'I need ___ details.'
Superlative of 'little' (amount):
Change to comparative: 'Iron is the most useful metal.'
options: Iron is more useful than any other metal.
Iron is as useful as metals.

questions.q: 'Of the two roads, take the ___.'
Which is correct?
'This is ___ useful ___ that.' (lower degree)
Positive form of 'Gold is more precious than silver':
options: Silver is not as precious as gold.
Gold is as precious as silver.

questions.q: Superlative of 'far' (distance):
Transform to superlative: 'No other festival in India is as colourful as Holi.'
options: Holi is more colourful than festivals.
Holi is the most colourful festival in India.
Holi is as colourful as festivals.
questions.explanation: 'No other … as … as' → superlative 'the most colourful'.

questions.q: Spot the error: 'She is more senior than me.'
questions.explanation: 'senior' takes 'to', and 'more' is redundant with it.

questions.q: Choose the parallel comparative: '___ he climbed, ___ the air became.'
questions.explanation: The 'the … the …' structure: 'The higher he climbed, the colder the air became.'

questions.q: Transform to comparative: 'Very few metals are as heavy as gold.'
options: Gold is heavier than most other metals.
Gold is as heavy as metals.
questions.explanation: 'Very few … as … as' → 'heavier than most other'.

questions.q: Identify the error: 'This book is more preferable than that.'
questions.explanation: 'preferable' already implies comparison; 'more' is wrong (use 'preferable to').

questions.q: Choose: 'He is the ___ of the two brothers.'
questions.explanation: When comparing only two, use the comparative with 'the': 'the taller'.

questions.q: Rearrange: 'than / city / any / cleaner / other / this / is'
options: This city is cleaner than any other.
This is cleaner city than any other.
Cleaner this city is than any other.
Than any other this city cleaner is.
questions.explanation: 'This city is cleaner than any other.' is correct.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly compares two things?
options: She is the cleverer of the two.
She is the cleverest of the two.
She is more cleverer of the two.
She is clever than the two.
questions.explanation: For two items, use the comparative with 'the': 'the cleverer of the two'.

outcomes: Use the three degrees of comparison accurately
Use structures like as…as, not as…as, less…than
Handle special pairs: elder/older, farther/further, latter/later
Transform a sentence between positive, comparative and superlative
Avoid double comparatives and faulty comparisons

intro.en: You already know tall, taller, tallest. This chapter goes further: how to compare with as…as, how to use tricky pairs like elder vs older, and — most importantly — how to rewrite the same idea in all three degrees without changing its meaning. That transformation skill is heavily tested in exams.
intro.hi: आप tall, taller, tallest पहले से जानते हैं। यह अध्याय आगे बढ़ता है: as…as से तुलना, elder बनाम older जैसे कठिन युग्म, और — सबसे महत्वपूर्ण — एक ही विचार को तीनों degrees में बिना अर्थ बदले दोबारा लिखना। यह transformation कौशल परीक्षाओं में खूब पूछा जाता है।

real_life.situation:
You compare two phones for a friend:

You: This one is not as expensive as that one, but no other phone in the shop is as fast as this. It is the best value here.
real_life.why: The same comparison appears in different forms — 'not as … as', 'as … as', and a superlative ('the best'). Being able to switch between these forms while keeping the meaning is exactly what this chapter trains.

rule_box.example: Iron is the most useful metal = Iron is more useful than any other metal = No other metal is as useful as iron.

quick_test.q: To change a superlative to a comparative, we usually add:
quick_test.explanation: 'the tallest' → 'taller than any other …' uses 'any other'.

common_mistakes.wrong: Iron is more useful than any metal.
common_mistakes.right: Iron is more useful than any other metal.
common_mistakes.note: Add 'other' when comparing within the same group.

common_mistakes.wrong: My older brother (meaning eldest in family, before noun is fine but 'elder' preferred).
common_mistakes.note: Use 'elder' for family relationships before a noun.

fill_l1.instructions: Complete with the correct degree of the adjective in brackets.

items.q: She is as ______ as her sister. (tall)
It is the ______ day of the year. (hot)
Delhi is ______ from here than Agra. (farther/further)
Of the two options, I prefer the ______. (later/latter)

error_detection.sentence: He is more stronger than Ravi.
Iron is more useful than any metal.
error_detection.correct: Iron is more useful than any other metal.

error_detection.sentence: She is the most tallest girl.
My older brother lives in Pune (family, before noun).
error_detection.correct: My elder brother lives in Pune.

sentence_correction.wrong: This is more better than that.
No other boy is so tall than Ravi.
sentence_correction.correct: No other boy is as tall as Ravi.

sentence_correction.wrong: Gold is the more precious of all metals.
sentence_correction.correct: Gold is the most precious of all metals.

rearrangement.jumbled: as / she / tall / as / is / him
rearrangement.answer: She is as tall as him.

answers: No other … as tall as → positive transformation

reading.passage: Of all the runners, Asha was the fastest. She was faster than any other girl in the school, and no other athlete trained as hard as she did. Her elder sister, who lived farther away, came to watch. "You are far better than last year," she said, "but there is always further room to improve."

questions.q: Rewrite 'Asha was the fastest' in the comparative degree.
questions.answer: Asha was faster than any other runner.

questions.q: Why is 'elder' used for the sister?
questions.answer: 'elder' is used for family relationships and comes before the noun 'sister'.

questions.q: Explain the difference between 'farther' and 'further' in the passage.
questions.answer: 'farther' = greater distance (lived farther away); 'further' = additional/more (further room to improve).

speaking: She is as intelligent as her brother.
This phone is better than that one.
Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
No other city is as crowded as Mumbai.
He is more hardworking than any other student.

writing.prompt: Write the same comparison in all three degrees for two of your favourite things (e.g. mango vs other fruits).
writing.example: Mango is the sweetest fruit. Mango is sweeter than any other fruit. No other fruit is as sweet as mango.

micro_quiz.q: Positive form of 'Ravi is taller than Sam':
options: Sam is not as tall as Ravi.
Ravi is as tall as Sam.

challenge.q: Change to comparative: 'No other planet is as large as Jupiter.'
options: Jupiter is larger than any other planet.
Jupiter is as large as planets.
Jupiter is more large than planets.
challenge.explanation: 'No other … as … as' → 'larger than any other'.

challenge.q: Identify the error: 'She is more wiser than her brother.'
Which transformation keeps the meaning of 'Health is the most important thing'?
options: Health is more important than any other thing.
Health is as important as wealth.
